tradition.label: Formal & physical sciences
tradition.definition: Wheel 1 (Sciences & engineering). Mathematics, theoretical physics and CS, logic, decision and game theory as foundations for understanding and aligning AI: singular learning theory, computational mechanics, category theory and verification, algorithmic information theory, agent foundations, game theory of cooperation, bargaining and races.

tradition.label: Life & systems sciences
tradition.definition: Wheel 2 (Sciences & engineering). Sciences of living and self-organising wholes: evolutionary and developmental biology, basal and collective intelligence, artificial life; neuroscience, NeuroAI, active inference, brain emulation; complexity; cybernetics, systems science, ecology, resilience; the systems strand of metacrisis thinking.

tradition.label: Consciousness & AI minds
tradition.definition: Wheel 3 (Minds & inner life). Consciousness science, sentience science and philosophy of mind applied to whether AI (and animals) have experience, welfare or moral status: indicators, welfare assessments, digital-minds field-building and governance, animal sentience bridged to AI, relational study of model minds.

tradition.label: Psychology & cognitive science
tradition.definition: Wheel 4 (Minds & inner life). Clinical psychology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis and peer support; child development; social, moral and wisdom psychology; relationships and affect; computational cognitive science and machine psychology; and coaching and applied-rationality services for AI-safety workers.

tradition.label: Contemplative & integral traditions
tradition.definition: Wheel 5 (Minds & inner life). First-person, practice-based traditions and their science: meditation and contemplative training, contemplative and compassion science, contemplative insight turned into AI design or alignment targets, and the integral, metamodern and inner-development milieu int/a comes from.

tradition.label: Religion & theology
tradition.definition: Wheel 6 (Minds & inner life). Organisations that speak from, for or to a religious tradition: churches, denominations, federations, interfaith bodies; theology, religious studies and religious law; faith media, investors, benchmarks and advocacy; chaplaincy; faith and science-and-religion funders.

tradition.label: Philosophy & ethics
tradition.definition: Wheel 7 (Humanities & cultures). Moral and political philosophy (longtermist, suffering-focused, virtue, care ethics), philosophy of technology and intelligence, continental and process thought, Chinese and African academic philosophy, applied ethics, bioethics and ethics councils.

tradition.label: Arts, narrative & futures
tradition.definition: Wheel 8 (Humanities & cultures). Imaginative and anticipatory disciplines: art, design and speculative design; narrative, literary and cultural studies; film, games, journalism and communications; futures studies and foresight (scenarios, Delphi, horizon scanning, wargames, technology assessment), incl. stories as model priors.

tradition.label: Indigenous & decolonial knowledges
tradition.definition: Wheel 9 (Humanities & cultures). Indigenous knowledge systems and data sovereignty (kinship ontologies, tikanga and kaitiakitanga, CARE principles, TK labels, Ubuntu-guided research) and decolonial, Black and feminist standpoint traditions that rebuild AI from marginalised communities' knowledge.

tradition.label: Law, rights & society
tradition.definition: Wheel 10 (Society & institutions). Law and legal theory (liability, human, children's and digital rights, whistleblowing, AI-rights advocacy), STS, sociology, anthropology, critical data studies, civil-society auditing, and public-interest, ELSI and development research and funding.

tradition.label: Economics, labour & commons
tradition.definition: Wheel 11 (Society & institutions). Economics of transformative AI (growth, labour, public finance, cash transfers), political economy and antitrust (power concentration, lock-in), commons, cooperatives and public-goods governance, and organised labour, incl. data workers.

tradition.label: Democracy & collective intelligence
tradition.definition: Wheel 12 (Society & institutions). Deliberative and participatory democracy (assemblies, deliberative polling, sortition, broad listening), collective-intelligence science and AI-for-democracy tools, and collective epistemics: forecasting, argument mapping, fact-checking, provenance, knowledge commons.

tradition.label: Peace, security & diplomacy
tradition.definition: Wheel 13 (Society & institutions). Nuclear risk and arms control, security studies and humanitarian law, Track II, science and multilateral diplomacy (incl. China studies), and peacebuilding, mediation and conflict transformation applied to AI and the AI race.

tradition.label: Safety & risk sciences
tradition.definition: Wheel 14 (Sciences & engineering), closing on Formal via verification. Safety-critical engineering and assurance (STAMP/STPA, safety cases, certification, standards), human factors, resilience engineering, incident reporting, risk management, insurance, infosec, catastrophe resilience, public health and biosecurity.

sub_tradition.label: Mathematics of learning
sub_tradition.definition: Mathematics, statistical physics, computational mechanics and category theory that explain learning or verify systems.

sub_tradition.label: Agents & game theory
sub_tradition.definition: Decision theory, algorithmic information theory, causal incentives, and game theory of cooperation, bargaining and races.

sub_tradition.label: Biology & diverse intelligence
sub_tradition.definition: Developmental and evolutionary biology, basal and animal cognition, collective behaviour, cultural evolution, artificial life.

sub_tradition.label: Neuroscience & NeuroAI
sub_tradition.definition: Systems and computational neuroscience, active inference, brain-inspired AGI, connectomics and whole-brain emulation.

sub_tradition.label: Complexity & emergence
sub_tradition.definition: Complexity science, information-theoretic emergence, network science and agent-based models of interacting agents.

sub_tradition.label: Cybernetics, systems & ecology
sub_tradition.definition: Cybernetics, systems theory, system dynamics, ecology and resilience science, and systems diagnoses of the metacrisis.

sub_tradition.label: Consciousness & sentience science
sub_tradition.definition: Theories, indicators and measurement of consciousness and sentience, philosophy of machine consciousness, animal sentience.

sub_tradition.label: AI welfare & status
sub_tradition.definition: AI welfare and moral-status research, model welfare assessments, public attitudes, readiness and the field's funders and networks.

sub_tradition.label: Relational study of minds
sub_tradition.definition: Studying language-model minds through sustained interaction, simulator theory, experimental writing and close reading.

sub_tradition.label: Clinical psychology & psychiatry
sub_tradition.definition: Psychiatry, psychotherapy, psychoanalysis, crisis practice and lived-experience peer support for AI-related harm.

sub_tradition.label: Child & youth development
sub_tradition.definition: Developmental psychology, paediatrics and youth work on how children and teens use AI, including ratings and funders.

sub_tradition.label: Social & wisdom psychology
sub_tradition.definition: Behavioural, social and moral psychology, persuasion, judgement, and the empirical science of wisdom and flourishing.

sub_tradition.label: Relationships & affect
sub_tradition.definition: Science of intimacy, attachment and emotion, and affective computing, as people form relationships with AI.

sub_tradition.label: Cognitive & machine psychology
sub_tradition.definition: Computational cognitive science, representational alignment, human-machine teaming and psychology experiments on models.

sub_tradition.label: Field health & coaching
sub_tradition.definition: Therapy referral, coaching, group mental-health programmes and applied rationality for AI-safety workers.

sub_tradition.label: Contemplative practice & retreat
sub_tradition.definition: Meditation, retreat, mindfulness and resilience training for AI builders, leaders, policymakers and publics.

sub_tradition.label: Contemplative science & AI
sub_tradition.definition: Contemplative and compassion science, and contemplative or Buddhist-philosophical insight turned into AI designs, models or evals.

sub_tradition.label: Integral & inner development
sub_tradition.definition: Integral theory, metamodernism, adult and inner development, awareness-based systems change, collective-trauma work.

sub_tradition.label: Christian traditions
sub_tradition.definition: Catholic, Protestant, evangelical and ecumenical churches, theologians and Christian institutions.

sub_tradition.label: Islamic & Jewish traditions
sub_tradition.definition: Islamic jurisprudence and theology (fiqh, maqasid, kalam) and Jewish law, thought and rabbinic bodies.

sub_tradition.label: Buddhist institutions
sub_tradition.definition: Buddhist federations, engaged-Buddhist networks, canon translation, ethics centres, magazines and funders.

sub_tradition.label: Interfaith & science-and-religion
sub_tradition.definition: Interreligious councils, science-and-religion bodies and funders, multi-faith evaluations, faith-based investors.

sub_tradition.label: Moral & political philosophy
sub_tradition.definition: Normative theory of value, agency, power and care, including longtermist and suffering-focused ethics.

sub_tradition.label: Philosophy of technology
sub_tradition.definition: Philosophy of technology and intelligence: continental, process, planetary and Chinese or African traditions.

sub_tradition.label: Applied ethics & councils
sub_tradition.definition: Bioethics, applied and virtue ethics, character education, ethics councils and engineering-ethics initiatives.

sub_tradition.label: Art & design
sub_tradition.definition: Visual and performing art, design research, speculative design and game design working with or on AI.

sub_tradition.label: Narrative, media & journalism
sub_tradition.definition: Narratology, literary and cultural studies, fiction, film, journalism, communications, narrative as model prior.

sub_tradition.label: Futures studies & foresight
sub_tradition.definition: Futures studies and foresight: scenarios, Delphi, horizon scanning, futures literacy, wargames, technology assessment.

sub_tradition.label: Indigenous data sovereignty
sub_tradition.definition: Indigenous-led research, protocols, licences and labels governing data and AI, and community-owned language technology.

sub_tradition.label: Decolonial, Black & feminist
sub_tradition.definition: Decolonial, Black and feminist research, design and speculative practice centring marginalised communities.

sub_tradition.label: Law & rights
sub_tradition.definition: Legal theory, liability, constitutional, human, children's and digital rights, whistleblowing, AI-rights advocacy.

sub_tradition.label: STS & critical sociology
sub_tradition.definition: STS, sociology, anthropology, media studies, critical data studies and civil-society algorithmic auditing.

sub_tradition.label: Public-interest, ELSI & development
sub_tradition.definition: Multidisciplinary public-interest, ELSI and development-studies institutes, networks and funders.

sub_tradition.label: Economics of transformative AI
sub_tradition.definition: Growth, labour economics, public finance and policy evaluation for AI-driven economic change.

sub_tradition.label: Political economy & antitrust
sub_tradition.definition: Political economy of power concentration and lock-in, competition law, anti-monopoly analysis and its funders.

sub_tradition.label: Commons & cooperatives
sub_tradition.definition: Commons governance, cooperatives, data cooperatives, public AI and public-goods funding mechanisms.

sub_tradition.label: Organised labour
sub_tradition.definition: Unions, worker organising, collective bargaining, fair-work standards, data workers and AI raters.

sub_tradition.label: Deliberative democracy
sub_tradition.definition: Citizens' assemblies, deliberative polling, sortition, participatory budgeting and popular public deliberation on AI.

sub_tradition.label: Collective intelligence tools
sub_tradition.definition: Collective-intelligence science and AI tools for opinion mapping, bridging and consensus.

sub_tradition.label: Forecasting & collective epistemics
sub_tradition.definition: Judgmental forecasting, epistemic evals, reasoning tools, fact-checking, provenance and knowledge commons.

sub_tradition.label: Arms control & IHL
sub_tradition.definition: Nuclear risk reduction, arms control, nonproliferation, security studies and humanitarian law.

sub_tradition.label: Track II & diplomacy
sub_tradition.definition: Scientist and expert dialogues, China studies, UN and regional diplomacy, elder statesmanship.

sub_tradition.label: Peacebuilding & mediation
sub_tradition.definition: Conflict transformation, private diplomacy, mediation and social cohesion, including AI-assisted dialogue.

sub_tradition.label: Safety engineering & assurance
sub_tradition.definition: Systems-theoretic safety, assurance cases, certification, standards, dependability, human factors, resilience engineering.

sub_tradition.label: Incidents, risk & insurance
sub_tradition.definition: Incident and vulnerability databases, quantitative risk, insurance, information security, national and catastrophe resilience.

sub_tradition.label: Public health & biosecurity
sub_tradition.definition: Health security, biosecurity evaluation, patient safety and clinical AI assurance.

ring.label: AI-safety core
ring.definition: Making advanced AI go well (alignment, safety, catastrophic or existential risk, AI welfare, governance of transformative AI) is the organisation's founding or primary mission; it belongs to the AI-safety and x-risk ecosystem (funded by, staffed from or listed by that community, often on the aisafety.com map); and it imports knowledge or methods from outside mainstream ML alignment and conventional AI policy. Includes AI-safety programmes inside frontier labs and national AI-safety institutes.

ring.label: Bridge from elsewhere
ring.definition: Rooted in another field or tradition (its people, institution, funding or identity belong there) and running a sustained, explicit programme on AI safety, catastrophic or existential risk, alignment, superintelligence, AI welfare or 'AI going well'. Sustained means a standing programme, funded project, fellowship, publication line or repeated convening in 2024-26, not a single event.

ring.label: Adjacent, no x-risk frame
ring.definition: Has a sustained AI programme rooted in another tradition, focused on AI's human, societal or cultural effects (harms, rights, wellbeing, labour, meaning, democracy, religion), without catastrophic-risk, alignment or 'AI going well' framing.

ring.label: Potential partner
ring.definition: Holds highly relevant knowledge, methods or reach, but its AI engagement is light (occasional events, essays, a single paper or session) or absent. The profiler must name, in one line, the transferable method that justifies inclusion.

problem.label: Understanding AI & agency
problem.definition: [The AI itself] A scientific or formal account of what AI systems are and do: how goals, agency, learning, world-models and capabilities arise, interpretability from physics, neuroscience, biology or cognitive science, and how agents could be designed differently.

problem.label: What AI should value
problem.definition: [The AI itself] The alignment target: which values, virtues, wisdom, care or character AI should have, and how to specify, train or evaluate for them from moral, contemplative, religious, Indigenous, developmental or narrative traditions.

problem.label: Assurance & oversight
problem.definition: [The AI itself] Making specific AI systems demonstrably safe and overseeable: evals and red-teaming, verification and safety cases, certification and standards, audits, incident reporting, human factors of oversight, insurance of deployed systems.

problem.label: Moral status of AI
problem.definition: [The AI itself] Whether AI systems are or could be subjects whose experiences matter, and what relationship follows: consciousness indicators, welfare assessments, digital-minds governance, relational study of model minds, AI-rights advocacy.

problem.label: Protecting minds & relationships
problem.definition: [Human minds & meaning] What AI does to human minds, development and relationships: companion harms, AI-associated psychosis and dependency, children's development, attention and cognitive liberty, manipulation and emulated empathy, sycophancy as harm, people's own agency.

problem.label: Meaning, dignity & formation
problem.definition: [Human minds & meaning] Humanity's moral and spiritual orientation to AI: what it means to be human, dignity and flourishing, moral and character formation, and the ethical voice of religious, humanist and contemplative communities to their members and publics.

problem.label: People doing the work
problem.definition: [Human minds & meaning] The people who build, govern, fund and make AI safe: wellbeing, inner development, practical wisdom, conscience, oaths, whistleblowing, worker voice in labs, and the data-labelling and rating workforce; also widening who does this work.

problem.label: Sensemaking, truth & foresight
problem.definition: [Living & deciding together] Whether people and institutions can see clearly with AI: forecasting, foresight and early warning, reasoning tools, model truthfulness, fact-checking, provenance, epistemic commons, information integrity, and how publics picture and narrate AI futures.

problem.label: Democratic voice & legitimacy
problem.definition: [Living & deciding together] How societies decide together about and with AI: assemblies and sortition, deliberative polling, public input into model behaviour, AI-assisted deliberation and bridging, collective intelligence, civil liberties, polycentric governance.

problem.label: Rights & plural voices
problem.definition: [Living & deciding together] Whose interests and voices count, and how developers are held to account: human-rights and liability law, bias and accountability audits, data and cultural sovereignty, Indigenous rights, Global South voice, feminist and decolonial alternatives.

problem.label: Power, wealth & work
problem.definition: [Living & deciding together] Who holds power and wealth as AI takes over labour and judgement: concentration and lock-in, gradual disempowerment, windfall distribution and TAI economics, competition policy, public AI, data ownership, labour as counter-power.

problem.label: Multi-agent AI & cooperation
problem.definition: [Cooperation, conflict & civilisation] Populations of interacting AI agents and the cooperation science that governs them: cooperative AI, collusion, bargaining and commitment, emergent collective behaviour, multi-agent security, game-theoretic models of AI races.

problem.label: Security & international coordination
problem.definition: [Cooperation, conflict & civilisation] Keeping states, militaries and developers from catastrophic conflict and misuse: military AI and nuclear escalation, autonomous weapons, bio and cyber misuse, influence operations, US-China and Track II dialogue, UN processes, treaties, red lines.

problem.label: Systemic risk & metacrisis
problem.definition: [Cooperation, conflict & civilisation] AI as one thread in civilisation's systemic predicament, and resilience when prevention fails: metacrisis and polycrisis, multipolar traps, planetary boundaries, catastrophe preparedness and recovery, infrastructure risk, long-term trajectory, future generations.

quadrant.label: Minds & experience (I)
quadrant.definition: The interior of individuals: experience, wellbeing, cognition as lived, development, character, contemplative states, and the possible interiority or welfare of AI systems.

quadrant.label: Meaning & culture (We)
quadrant.definition: Shared interiors: values, ethics, religion, narratives, culture, intersubjective understanding, dialogue and deliberation as meaning-making.

quadrant.label: Mechanisms & machines (It)
quadrant.definition: The observable structure and behaviour of single systems: AI models and agents (internals, behaviour, evaluations, training data), brains and organisms, engineered artefacts and their verification.

quadrant.label: Systems & structures (Its)
quadrant.definition: Collective exteriors: institutions, law, markets, geopolitics, ecosystems of interacting agents, and complex social and ecological systems.

role.label: Research & theory
role.definition: Produces original studies, theory or analysis that change what the field thinks is true or possible.

role.label: Measure & evaluate
role.definition: Benchmarks, evals, audits, red-teaming, ratings, indices, surveys, incident databases and forecasts that make a problem visible and trackable.

role.label: Build tools & alternatives
role.definition: Software, datasets, infrastructure, prototypes, products or alternative AI systems that embody a different way of doing things.

role.label: Set norms & standards
role.definition: Principles, codes, technical standards, certification, design codes, labels, professional oaths and religious rulings that define acceptable practice.

role.label: Law, policy & advocacy
role.definition: Litigation, legislation, regulatory advice, treaty campaigns and advocacy aimed at governments or courts.

role.label: Convene & mediate
role.definition: Dialogues, Track II channels, summits, conferences, workshops and brokering that build trust or shared understanding between groups that do not otherwise meet.

role.label: Widen participation
role.definition: Participatory, deliberative or sovereignty-based processes that give affected or excluded people real say.

role.label: Organise collective power
role.definition: Unions, coalitions, campaigns, movements and shareholder action that put collective pressure on developers or governments.

role.label: Educate & form
role.definition: Courses, schools, fellowships with teaching, trainings, retreats and character or contemplative formation that change people's capacities.

role.label: Care & support
role.definition: Direct psychological, spiritual, peer, coaching or legal support to individuals.

role.label: Media, art & storytelling
role.definition: Journalism, publishing, newsletters, podcasts, film, art, scenarios and serious games for public or decision-maker audiences.

role.label: Fund others
role.definition: Grants, fellowships, prizes and pooled funds that resource other organisations.

org_type.label: Independent nonprofit
org_type.definition: Independent nonprofit, charity, NGO or think tank, including independent research institutes.

org_type.label: Academic centre or lab
org_type.definition: University centre, lab, institute or research group, and units of public research organisations (Max Planck, Fraunhofer, DLR).

org_type.label: Hosted programme or project
org_type.definition: A programme, project, consortium, workshop series or strand inside a host organisation, or a time-limited funded project.

org_type.label: Funder or fund
org_type.definition: Foundation, pooled fund, grant programme or philanthropic investor whose main AI activity is funding.

org_type.label: Network or coalition
org_type.definition: Open network, alliance, coalition, movement or online community without formal individual membership dues.

org_type.label: Membership body
org_type.definition: Union, professional association, learned society, standards community with members, or religious denomination or federation acting for its members.

org_type.label: Company or startup
org_type.definition: For-profit company, public-benefit corporation or studio.

org_type.label: Publication or media
org_type.definition: Magazine, journal, newsletter, podcast or media production organisation.

org_type.label: Public or intergovernmental body
org_type.definition: Government agency, statutory council or commissioner, national AI-safety institute, or UN, OECD, OIC or EU body.

transfer.label: Into the model
transfer.definition: The tradition's knowledge is applied to AI systems themselves: training data, internals, agent design, model specs or evaluations aimed at model behaviour.

transfer.label: Into the builders
transfer.definition: The tradition's practices reach the people who build, govern or fund AI, as people: wellbeing, formation, conscience, oaths, whistleblowing support, organising inside labs.

transfer.label: Into institutions
transfer.definition: The tradition supplies templates for governing AI: dialogues and treaties, safety cases, incident systems, liability, standards, deliberative processes, collective bargaining, policy designs.

transfer.label: Protecting its constituency
transfer.definition: The tradition studies or defends the people it already serves (children, patients, workers, believers, Indigenous communities) from AI's effects.

transfer.label: Convening its community
transfer.definition: The tradition brings its own community into the AI conversation: dialogues, summits, education, literacy, media for its members.

transfer.label: None yet
transfer.definition: Ring = potential and no AI work at all: the tradition holds relevant knowledge that has not moved.

framing.label: Catastrophic or existential
framing.definition: Extreme or irreversible outcomes: loss of control, mass-casualty misuse, nuclear escalation, s-risks, or moral catastrophe at scale (including mass digital suffering).

framing.label: Structural and gradual
framing.definition: Systemic erosion without a single catastrophe: disempowerment, lock-in, power concentration, epistemic decay, rivalrous dynamics.

framing.label: Present, concrete harms
framing.definition: Harms to identifiable people or groups now: rights violations, bias, child safety, labour exploitation, psychological injury.

framing.label: Flourishing and positive
framing.definition: Aspirational: what a good outcome is and how to reach it (wisdom, flourishing, care, positive futures) as the main aim.

framing.label: Critical or deflationary
framing.definition: Sceptical or deflationary about AI capabilities, AI consciousness or x-risk discourse itself, as its main output.

way_of_knowing.label: Formal & mathematical
way_of_knowing.definition: Knowledge as proof, formal model or simulation.

way_of_knowing.label: Empirical & experimental
way_of_knowing.definition: Knowledge from experiment, measurement, surveys and field data.

way_of_knowing.label: Professional & clinical practice
way_of_knowing.definition: Codified practitioner knowledge: engineering assurance, clinical care, mediation, diplomacy, facilitation, standards.

way_of_knowing.label: Interpretive & normative
way_of_knowing.definition: Knowledge from argument, textual and legal interpretation, ethical reasoning and critique.

way_of_knowing.label: Contemplative & embodied
way_of_knowing.definition: First-person, somatic, meditative and phenomenological knowing.

way_of_knowing.label: Communal & lived
way_of_knowing.definition: Knowledge held by a community: Indigenous knowledge, lived experience of harm, organised workers, participatory process.

way_of_knowing.label: Imaginative & creative
way_of_knowing.definition: Knowledge through art, narrative, design, scenarios and play.

region.label: North America
region.definition: Headquartered in the US or Canada.

region.label: UK & Ireland
region.definition: Headquartered in the UK or Ireland.

region.label: Continental Europe
region.definition: Headquartered in continental Europe, including Switzerland and the Nordics.

region.label: Asia-Pacific
region.definition: East, South, Southeast and Central Asia, Australia, Aotearoa New Zealand and the Pacific.

region.label: Latin America & Caribbean
region.definition: Headquartered in Latin America or the Caribbean.

region.label: Middle East, North Africa
region.definition: Headquartered in the Middle East or North Africa.

region.label: Global or distributed
region.definition: Distributed online, or a federation or network with no single base.

standpoint.label: Indigenous-led
standpoint.definition: Led by Indigenous people or governed by Indigenous communities.

standpoint.label: Majority World
standpoint.definition: Led from, or centred on, Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, South, Southeast or Central Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, or the Pacific Islands. A Northern host's programme counts only if it is led locally.

inta_hub.label: London
inta_hub.definition: Office, team or regular (at least quarterly) in-person activity in London.

inta_hub.label: Berlin
inta_hub.definition: Office, team or regular in-person activity in Berlin.

inta_hub.label: Paris
inta_hub.definition: Office, team or regular in-person activity in Paris.

inta_hub.label: Joinable online
inta_hub.definition: A recurring programme, dialogue series or community that anyone eligible can join remotely.

engagement.label: Staff roles
engagement.definition: Employs research or programme staff (check the site for current openings).

engagement.label: Fellowships & residencies
engagement.definition: Runs recurring fellowships, scholarships, residencies or summer institutes.

engagement.label: Open funding calls
engagement.definition: Runs open RFPs, challenges or grant rounds.

engagement.label: Events & retreats
engagement.definition: Public conferences, summits or retreats with an AI strand.

engagement.label: Courses & trainings
engagement.definition: Courses or trainings open to applicants or the public.

engagement.label: Communities to join
engagement.definition: Open networks, online communities and practitioner hubs.

engagement.label: Open contribution
engagement.definition: Volunteering, red-teaming, submitting cases or data, rating notes or mapping arguments.

engagement.label: Door to open
engagement.definition: Holds relevant methods but has no AI programme yet, so it needs outreach from a founder, funder or researcher who wants to partner.

status.label: Newly launched
status.definition: Launched in 2025-26, so the track record is short.

status.label: Dormant or closed
status.definition: Closed, in maintenance mode, dormant, or with a lapsed web presence; its niche may be open.

status.label: Pivoted or renamed
status.definition: Has changed mission, ownership or name, or now operates commercially.

status.label: Needs verification
status.definition: Sources conflict or the public site is minimal.

badges.label: Full-spectrum knowing
badges.definition: Uses embodied, contemplative, artistic, Indigenous or experiential knowing alongside rigorous analysis, as method.

badges.label: Speed of wisdom
badges.definition: Practises explicit discernment about pace: pause or slow-technology positions, de-escalation, refusing race or power-seeking dynamics.

badges.label: Decoupling & recoupling
badges.definition: Analyses AI risk on its own and also inside the wider metacrisis and its systemic interconnections.

badges.label: Fractal altruism
badges.definition: Pairs scope-sensitive ambition with local, community-rooted and intrinsic values.

badges.label: Inner work, outer change
badges.definition: Explicitly couples the inner development of practitioners with outer change in AI.

tradition.name: Tradition (home + secondary)
tradition.question: Which body of knowledge, practice or tradition does it bring to making AI go well? First value = home (exactly one); then 0-2 traditions it also draws on substantially (3 for hubs, up to 4 for generalist funders).

sub_tradition.name: Sub-tradition
sub_tradition.question: Within its home tradition, which recognisable school or community is it part of?

ring.name: Ring of proximity
ring.question: How close is it to the AI-safety core?

problem.name: Problem addressed
problem.question: Which parts of 'making the transition to advanced AI go well' does its work bear on? (1-3 values; the first is the primary problem.)

quadrant.name: Integral quadrant
quadrant.question: Which dimensions of reality does its AI work attend to and try to change: inner experience, shared meaning, observable mechanisms, or collective systems? (1-2 values; first is main.)

role.name: Role
role.question: What does the organisation actually do, and how does it expect that to make a difference? (1-3 values, main first.)

org_type.name: Organisation type
org_type.question: What kind of organisation is the roster entry?

transfer.name: Direction of transfer
transfer.question: What actually flows from its tradition into the AI transition: who or what changes because of its work?

framing.name: Risk framing
framing.question: How does it frame what is at stake, in its own words?

way_of_knowing.name: Way of knowing
way_of_knowing.question: What kind of knowledge does its main AI output contribute?

standpoint.name: Majority-World standpoint
standpoint.question: Is it Indigenous-led, or led from or centred on the Majority World?

inta_hub.name: Near an int/a hub
inta_hub.question: Is it present near int/a's communities in London, Berlin or Paris, or joinable online? (0-4 values.)

engagement.name: How to engage
engagement.question: How can a person or funder get involved: work, apply, attend, join, contribute or partner?

status.name: Status
status.question: Is it active, new, dormant, changed or unverified?

badges.name: int/a principle badges
badges.question: Does it exemplify one of int/a's principles unusually clearly? (Sparse; 0-2 values.)
